materialDomain.title: EMaterialDomain
materialDomain.description:
The domain that the material's attributes will be evaluated in.
Certain pieces of material functionality are only valid in certain domains, for example vertex normal is only valid on a surface.

blendMode.title: EBlendMode
blendMode.description: Determines how the material's color is blended with background colors.

materialDecalResponse.title: EMaterialDecalResponse
materialDecalResponse.description:
Defines how the material reacts on DBuffer decals (Affects look, performance and texture/sample usage).
Non DBuffer Decals can be disabled on the primitive (e.g. static mesh)

naniteOverrideMaterial.title: MaterialOverrideNanite
naniteOverrideMaterial.description: An override material which will be used instead of this one when rendering with Nanite.

overrideMaterialEditor.title: /Script/Engine.MaterialInterface
overrideMaterialEditor.description:
EditorOnly version of the OverrideMaterial reference.
This is a hard reference, but is editoronly. We rely on -skiponlyeditoronly to avoid pulling this editoronly hard reference into the cook.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

startSizePixels.description:
How large the max displacement should be, in on-screen pixels, when beginning to fade out displacement.
NOTE: This should be a LARGER number than End Fade Size.

endSizePixels.description:
How large the max displacement should be, in on-screen pixels, when fading out should complete, and displacement
should be disabled.
NOTE: This should be a SMALLER number than Start Fade Size.

shadingModel.title: EMaterialShadingModel
shadingModel.description: Determines how inputs are combined to create the material's final color.

bCastDynamicShadowAsMasked.description: Whether the material should cast shadows as masked even though it has a translucent blend mode.

usedShadingModels.description: These are the shading models present in this material. Note that all these shading models might not be used in all feature levels and quality levels.

opacityMaskClipValue.description:
If BlendMode is BLEND_Masked, the surface is not rendered where OpacityMask < OpacityMaskClipValue.
If BlendMode is BLEND_Translucent, BLEND_Additive, or BLEND_Modulate, and "Output Depth and Velocity" is enabled,
the object velocity is not rendered where Opacity < OpacityMaskClipValue.

bEnableResponsiveAA.description:
Indicates that the material should be rendered using responsive anti-aliasing. Improves sharpness of small moving particles such as sparks.
Only use for small moving features because it will cause aliasing of the background.

twoSided.description: Indicates that the material should be rendered without backface culling and the normal should be flipped for backfaces.

bIsThinSurface.description: Indicates that the material should be rendered as a thin surface (i.e., without inner volume). Only used by Substrate materials. Enabling ThinSurface will disable subsurface profiles.

ditheredLODTransition.description: Whether meshes rendered with the material should support dithered LOD transitions.

ditherOpacityMask.description: Dither opacity mask. When combined with Temporal AA this can be used as a form of limited translucency which supports all lighting features.

bAllowNegativeEmissiveColor.description: Whether the material should allow outputting negative emissive color values.  Only allowed on unlit materials.

bHasPixelAnimation.description:
Whether the opaque material has any pixel animations happening, that isn't included in the geometric velocities.
This allows to disable renderer's heuristics that assumes animation is fully described with motion vector, such as TSR's anti-flickering heuristic.

bEnableTessellation.description: Whether tessellation is enabled on the material. NOTE: Required for displacement to work.

bEnableDisplacementFade.description: Enables fading out and disabling of dynamic displacement in the distance, as displacement becomes unnoticeable

translucencyPass.title: EMaterialTranslucencyPass
translucencyPass.description:
Specifies the separate pass in which to render translucency.
This can be used to avoid artifacts caused by certain post processing effects.

translucencyLightingMode.title: ETranslucencyLightingMode
translucencyLightingMode.description: Sets the lighting mode that will be used on this material if it is translucent.

bEnableMobileSeparateTranslucency.description: Indicates that the translucent material should not be affected by bloom or DOF. (Note: Depth testing is not available)

numCustomizedUVs.description: Number of customized UV inputs to display.  Unconnected customized UV inputs will just pass through the vertex UVs.

translucencyDirectionalLightingIntensity.description:
Useful for artificially increasing the influence of the normal on the lighting result for translucency.
A value larger than 1 increases the influence of the normal, a value smaller than 1 makes the lighting more ambient.

translucentShadowDensityScale.description: Scale used to make translucent shadows more or less opaque than the material's actual opacity.

translucentSelfShadowDensityScale.description:
Scale used to make translucent self-shadowing more or less opaque than the material's shadow on other objects.
This is only used when the object is casting a volumetric translucent shadow.

translucentSelfShadowSecondDensityScale.description: Used to make a second self shadow gradient, to add interesting shading in the shadow of the first.

translucentSelfShadowSecondOpacity.description: Controls the strength of the second self shadow gradient.

translucentBackscatteringExponent.description:
Controls how diffuse the material's backscattering is when using the MSM_Subsurface shading model.
Larger exponents give a less diffuse look (smaller, brighter backscattering highlight).
This is only used when the object is casting a volumetric translucent shadow from a directional light.

translucentMultipleScatteringExtinction.title: LinearColor
translucentMultipleScatteringExtinction.description:
Colored extinction factor used to approximate multiple scattering in dense volumes.
This is only used when the object is casting a volumetric translucent shadow.

translucentShadowStartOffset.description: Local space distance to bias the translucent shadow.  Positive values move the shadow away from the light.

bDisableDepthTest.description: Whether to draw on top of opaque pixels even if behind them. This only has meaning for translucency.

bWriteOnlyAlpha.description: Whether the transluency pass should write its alpha, and only the alpha, into the framebuffer

bGenerateSphericalParticleNormals.description: Whether to generate spherical normals for particles that use this material.

bTangentSpaceNormal.description:
Whether the material takes a tangent space normal or a world space normal as input.
(TangentSpace requires extra instructions but is often more convenient).

bUseEmissiveForDynamicAreaLighting.description: If enabled, the material's emissive colour is injected into the LightPropagationVolume

bSubstrateRoughnessTracking.description: This can be used to disable roughness tracking. When this is done, top layers roughness will no longer impact bottom layer roughness.

bUsedWithLidarPointCloud.description:
Indicates that the material and its instances can be use with LiDAR Point Clouds
This will result in the shaders required to support LiDAR Point Cloud geometries being compiled which will increase shader compile time and memory usage.

bForceCompatibleWithLightFunctionAtlas.description:
Indicates that this material is safe to use with the light function atlas:
 - texture coordinates are manipulated in a way that works.
 - world position and depth are not used in the graph or do work with the atlas.
Forces all deferred lights to go the fast batched lighting code path (no screen shadow mask).

bAutomaticallySetUsageInEditor.description:
Whether to automatically set usage flags on this material or its instances based on what they are applied to in the editor.
Note that adding usage flags accidentally can add unwanted shader permutations.

bFullyRough.description: Forces the material to be completely rough. Saves a number of instructions and one sampler.

floatPrecisionMode.title: EMaterialFloatPrecisionMode
floatPrecisionMode.description:
Per Material override to change floating point precision in the pixel shader (ALU and uniforms precision)
Full-precision (highp) is slower than (half-precision/mediump) but can be used to work around precision-related rendering errors.
Use:
'Default' to take the precision set by the project wide cvar r.Mobile.FloatPrecisionMode. It defaults to 0 (half precision)
'Full-precision for MaterialExpressions only' if you still want to keep half precision in.ush/.usf shaders (global shaders)
'Full-precision for every float' to force every float and uniform to full-precision
'Half-precision' to try to use half precision ALU and uniforms where appropriate
'Half-precision including shader parameters' same behaviour as 'Half-precision' but it also uses half precision for uniforms with custom parameters like PreshaderBuffer uniform

bUseLightmapDirectionality.description: Use lightmap directionality and per pixel normals. If disabled, lighting from lightmaps will be flat but cheaper.

bUseAlphaToCoverage.description: Use alpha to coverage for masked material on mobile, make sure MSAA is enabled as well.

bForwardRenderUsePreintegratedGFForSimpl.description: Forward (including mobile) renderer: use preintegrated GF lut for simple IBL, but will use one more sampler.

bUseHQForwardReflections.description: Forward renderer: enables multiple parallax-corrected reflection captures that blend together.

bForwardBlendsSkyLightCubemaps.description: Enables blending of sky light cubemap textures. When disabled, the secondary cubemap is only visible when the blend factor is 1.

bUsePlanarForwardReflections.description: Enables planar reflection when using the forward renderer or mobile. Enabling this setting reduces the number of samplers available to the material as one more sampler will be used for the planar reflection.

bNormalCurvatureToRoughness.description: Reduce roughness based on screen space normal changes.

allowTranslucentCustomDepthWrites.description: Allows a translucent material to be used with custom depth writing by compiling additional shaders.

bAllowFrontLayerTranslucency.description: Allows a translucent material to be used with Front Layer Translucency by compiling additional shaders. Useful for controlling what should be included in Front Layer Translucency.

bCompatibleWithLumenCardSharing.description: When true, allows to share Lumen Cards between different instances even when material uses world position or per instance data, which may change material look per instance. All materials on a component needs this flag set for sharing to work.

wireframe.description: Enables a wireframe view of the mesh the material is applied to.

bAllowTranslucentLocalLightShadow.description: Allows a translucent material to receive local light shadows.

translucentLocalLightShadowQuality.description: Set local light shadow quality received by translucent material.

translucentDirectionalLightShadowQuality.description: Set directional light shadow quality received by translucent material.

shadingRate.title: EMaterialShadingRate
shadingRate.description:
Select what shading rate to apply, on platforms that support variable rate shading.
Non-1x1 rates will reduce the rasterization fidelity for the material; they will not super-sample the material.
This can save GPU performance on materials where reduced fidelity is acceptable.

bAllowVariableRateShading.description: Allows the use of variable rate shading when evaluating this material. This will only apply to the base/translucency pass.

bUseMaterialAttributes.description: when true, the material attributes pin is used instead of the regular pins.

bEnableNewHLSLGenerator.description: when true, the new material translator is used to translate this material

bCastRayTracedShadows.description: when true, the material casts ray tracing shadows.

bUseTranslucencyVertexFog.description: When true, translucent materials are fogged. Defaults to true.

bApplyCloudFogging.description: When true, translucent materials receive cloud contribution as part of the fog evaluation, per vertex or per pixel according to the other selected options. This is a rough approximation but can help in some cases. Defaults to false. Fog is applied on clouds, so Apply Fogging must be true to use this feature.

bIsSky.description: Unlit and Opaque materials can be used as sky material on a sky dome mesh. When IsSky is true, these meshes will not receive any contribution from the aerial perspective. Height and Volumetric fog effects will still be applied.

bComputeFogPerPixel.description: When true, translucent materials have fog computed for every pixel, which costs more but fixes artifacts due to low tessellation.

bOutputTranslucentVelocity.description: When true, translucent materials will output motion vectors and write to depth buffer in velocity pass.

bIsTranslucencyVelocityFromDepth.description:
When true, translucent materials that write velocity will calculate it only based on the written depth and camera movement.
This can be useful for translucent volume raycasts which write pixel depth offset and want to calculate velocity based on the output depth.

bRelaxRuntimeVirtualTextureRestrictions.description:
Relax restrictions on Runtime Virtual Texture output compilation.
Normally we give a compilation error whenever a Runtime Virtual Texture Output reads from a Virtual Texture.
This is because there is no feedback from Runtime Virtual Texture Output passes and no guarantee that Virtual Textures will be ready.
If allowed then Runtime Virtual Texture pages can contain stale low resolution data that is not evicted until the pages are flushed.

blendableLocation.title: EBlendableLocation
blendableLocation.description: Where the node is inserted in the (post processing) graph, only used if domain is PostProcess

blendableOutputAlpha.description: If this is enabled, the blendable will output alpha

userSceneTexture.description: Specify a user generated scene texture as output, overriding the default output implied by "Blendable Location", only used if domain is PostProcess

userTextureDivisor.title: IntPoint
userTextureDivisor.description: A divisor for the resolution of the User Scene Texture above, allowing an intermediate with reduced resolution

resolutionRelativeToInput.description: Set output resolution relative to the given User Scene Texture input.  Negative User Texture Divisors upsample (clamped at full resolution).

bDisablePreExposureScale.description:
Disable pre-exposure scale in post process materials (multiply by View.OneOverPreExposure on inputs, View.PreExposure on output).  Useful for
materials that don't care about the absolute intensity of SceneColor (for example, a blur), simplifying custom HLSL and saving some performance.
Or useful for non-color UserSceneTextures (for example, mask, matte, modulation, offset, or ID textures), where pre-exposure scale is
undesirable.  Pre-exposure scale can be manually reapplied via custom HLSL if needed on specific inputs or the output.

bEnableStencilTest.description:
Selectively execute post process material only for pixels that pass the stencil test against the Custom Depth/Stencil buffer.
Pixels that fail the stencil test are filled with the previous post process material output or scene color.

neuralProfileId.description: Set by reference object cannot be modified.

refractionMethod.title: ERefractionMode
refractionMethod.description: Controls how the Refraction input is interpreted and how the refraction offset into scene color is computed for this material.

refractionCoverageMode.title: ERefractionCoverageMode
refractionCoverageMode.description: Controls whether refraction takes into account the material surface coverage, or not. This is only for when substrate FrontMaterial is plugged in, not legacy root node material for the sake of compatibility.

pixelDepthOffsetMode.title: EPixelDepthOffsetMode
pixelDepthOffsetMode.description: Controls whether refraction takes into account the material surface coverage, or not.

blendablePriority.description: If multiple nodes with the same  type are inserted at the same point, this defined order and if they get combined, only used if domain is PostProcess

bIsBlendable.description: Allows blendability to be turned off, only used if domain is PostProcess

preshaderGap.description: If non-zero, overrides r.Material.PreshaderGapInterval for this material.  Workaround for a platform specific register overflow bug.

refractionDepthBias.description: This is the refraction depth bias, larger values offset distortion to prevent closer objects from rendering into the distorted surface at acute viewing angles but increases the disconnect between surface and where the refraction starts.

maxWorldPositionOffsetDisplacement.description:
Specifies the max world position offset of the material. Use this value to resolve issues with culling and self-occlusion caused by
World Position Offset, and/or to restrict how much offset is permitted (i.e. values are clamped on each axis).
NOTE: A value of 0.0 effectively means "no maximum", and will not clamp the offsets, however it will also not extend culling bounds.

bAlwaysEvaluateWorldPositionOffset.description:
Forces World Position Offset to always be evaluated for this material, even if the primitive it's applied to has disabled it
via "Evaluate World Position Offset" or "World Position Offset Disable Distance".
